title: Photoactivated Localization Microscopy with Bimolecular Fluorescence Complementation (BiFC-PALM)
protocol: Determine the configurations to clone and choose a linker.
Tag proteins with the fragments on the N- or C-terminus so they do not disrupt proper localization.
Use a flexible linker such as (GGGGS)x2.
Genetically tag the proteins of interest to PAmCherry1 fragments RN and RC.
Linearize plasmids containing fragments RN and RC with inverse PCR at the point of insertion.

Mix the PCR reaction together, bringing up to a final volume of 50 µl: add water, 25 µl of 2x master mix, 0.5 µl each of forward and reverse primers (final concentration 0.2 µM), and 1 ng template DNA.
Use cycling conditions: 98 °C for 30 sec, followed by 30 cycles of 98 °C for 7 sec and 68 °C for 2 min each cycle, with a final extension at 72 °C for 10 min.
PCR the genes of interest for insertion to the linearized plasmids containing RN and RC fragments.
Perform PCR with an extension time at 68 °C.
Use primers with overhangs that contain a flexible linker sequence, such as GGAGGTGGAGGTAGTGGTGGAGGTGGAAGT for (GGGGS)x2.
Include 15 base pair homology to the ends of the linearized RN and RC plasmids for recombination.
Digest the PCR reaction with Dpn1 to eliminate the PCR template.
Add 0.5 µl of Dpn1 (20 U/µl) directly to the 50 µl of PCR reaction.
Incubate at 37 °C for 1 hr and heat inactivate at 80 °C for 20 min.
Increase enzyme amount or lengthen digestion time if background template persists in later steps.
Purify the PCR products via a spin column as described by the manufacturer.
Measure the concentration of the purified PCR products.
Combine 50 ng of linearized plasmid and 50 ng of the gene of interest with 1 µl of enzyme premix.
Bring the total volume to 5 µl with deionized water.
Incubate at 50 °C for 15 min, place on ice, and add 20 µl of TE buffer.
Transform recombinant plasmids into competent bacteria.
Select colonies for O/N culture.
Add 5 ml of LB broth into a polypropylene round-bottom tube.
Add 5 μl of kanamycin (50 mg/ml stock) to the tube.
Inoculate the selected bacteria colony with a sterilized inoculating loop.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight while shaking at 225 rpm.
Freeze 1 ml of O/N culture for glycerol stock.
Miniprep the remainder as described by the manufacturer.
Perform sequencing to determine a good clone.
Use M13 forward and reverse primers (in separate reactions) if necessary.
Compare with the expected sequence using an alignment tool such as BLAST from NCBI.
Transfer the sequence-verified constructs to an expression plasmid via a recombinase reaction.
Add 75 ng of the destination plasmid to the enzyme premix.
Add 50 ng of the recombinant cloning plasmid to the mixture.
Bring up the total volume to 5 μl with deionized water.
Incubate at 25 °C for 1 hr.
Add 5 μl of TE buffer.
Transform 5 μl into competent bacteria and miniprep the plasmids as in steps 1.2.6 to 1.2.8, but using the appropriate antibiotic (typically ampicillin).
Add 350 µl of phenol red-free and antibiotic-free DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS into each well of an 8-well #1.5 glass bottom chamber slide.
Plate about 7.5 x 10^4 cells per well so cells are about 70%-90% confluent the next day.
Co-transfect expression plasmids with different configurations in each well using the preferred reagent and as described by the manufacturer.
For each well, add 125 ng of each expression plasmid into 50 µl of serum-free reduced media in a 0.6 ml tube and pipette up and down to mix.
Add 1 µl of the transfection reagent down the center of the tube and directly into the media.
Agitate gently to mix and let the reaction sit for 30 min.
Reduce the media in each well of the chamber slide by about half.
Add the transfection mixture dropwise to the wells.
Shake gently to mix.
Incubate cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 24-48 hours.
Change the media the day after transfection.
Image cells on a fluorescence microscope as in Protocol 2 beginning with step 2.1.4.
Create a negative control by introducing a point mutation into one of the proteins of interest that disrupts the interaction.
Perform site-directed mutagenesis on the cloning plasmid of the protein to be mutated and of the chosen configuration.
Generate a stable cell line by packaging constructs into viral particles.
Infect U2OS cells (or cell line of choice) with the packaged viruses.
Consider an inducible (tetracycline) expression system for controlled expression.
Plate about 2 x 10^6 293T/17 cells into a 10 cm dish per construct to be packaged.
Prepare a transfection reaction using a transfection reagent of choice.
Mix packaging plasmids in sterile water at final concentrations of 250 ng/µl for plasmid 1 and 2, and 100 ng/µl for plasmid 3.
Add 10 µl of the premixed packaging plasmids to 1 ml of serum-free reduced media in a 5 ml tube.
Add 2.5 µg of target plasmid to the media in the tube.
Mix up and down to combine all components thoroughly.
Add 20 µl of transfection reagent directly into the media in the center of the tube.
Agitate gently to mix.
Incubate at RT for 30 min.
Remove about half the media from the cells.
Add the transfection mixture dropwise into the media.
Shake gently to mix.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Incubate 10 ml of media per plate in a tube with the cap loosened for temperature and CO2 equilibration.
Gently change the media with pre-incubated media on Day 3.
Return the cells to the incubator after changing media.
Tilt the pipettor horizontally and add media dropwise into one edge of the plate when changing media.
Harvest the virus by removing the media with a syringe and filtering through a 0.45 µm pore size filter into a clean 50 ml tube on Day 4.
Gently replace the media with pre-incubated media after harvesting the virus.
Harvest again as done previously in step 1.5.3.3 and combine common filtrate into the same 50 ml tube on Day 5.
Add 6 ml of virus concentrator to each tube and mix.
Store at 4 °C for at least 24 hours until the virus precipitates.
Concentrate the virus by centrifuging at 1,500 x g for 15 minutes at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 250 μl of media.
Plate about 3 × 10^5 U2OS (or target) cells per well into a 6-well plate (2 ml of DMEM with 0.1% FBS per well) to achieve about 50% confluence at the time of infection.
The following day, remove approximately half the media so that about 1 ml remains in each well.
Coinfect with 50 μl of concentrated virus for each construct.
Add 1 μl of polybrene (8 mg/ml) to each well.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Change the medium the next day and incubate for one more day before adding antibiotics for selection.
Separate wells with uninfected cells are required as control samples to test the efficacy of the antibiotic selection.
Incubate for 2-7 days, or until the selection is complete.
Add effective concentrations of antibiotics (typically 1.0 μg/ml for puromycin and 1.0 mg/ml for neomycin) to select for infected cells.
Expand selected cells into a larger 10 cm dish and proceed to Protocol 2.
Prepare a sample for imaging by cleaning an 8-well #1.5 glass-bottom chamber slide with 250 μl of 1 M NaOH for at least 1 hour.
Thoroughly wash the slide with PBS after cleaning.
Plate about 5.5 x 10^4 U2OS stable expression cells per well in 350 μl of phenol red-free DMEM with 10% FBS.
Incubate the cleaned chamber slide with PBS overnight after washing if necessary.
Perform necessary treatments for the experiment, such as adding tetracycline to induce protein expression.
Prepare fresh paraformaldehyde (PFA) solution — mix 3.7 g of PFA in 1 ml of distilled water and 30 μl of 1 M NaOH.
Heat the mixture at 70 °C until completely dissolved, vortexing every 1-2 minutes.
Transfer the dissolved PFA to a 15 ml conical tube and add 3.8 ml distilled water, 5 ml 2x PHEM buffer, and 20 μl of 25% glutaraldehyde.
Vortex the solution to mix thoroughly.
Fix the cells immediately before imaging with the prepared PFA solution.
Remove the growth medium from the cells.
Wash the cells quickly with 500 µl of PBS.
Add 250 µl of PFA fixative per well.
Incubate the cells for 20 min at room temperature.
Remove the PFA fixative from the sample.
Add 350 µl of PBS or imaging buffer per well.
Vortex 100 nm gold particles to break up aggregates.
Add 35 µl of gold particle solution per well (10x final dilution).
Turn on the microscope.
Power on the 405 and 561 nm lasers, but keep shutters closed initially.
Turn on the EMCCD camera and allow it to cool down.
Ensure the 561 nm filters are in place.
Set the exposure time to 100 msec in the acquisition software.
Set the EMCCD gain to 300.
Add immersion oil to the objective.
Secure the sample to the microscope stage.
Focus the sample using bright field or the 561 nm laser.
Use a 60X apochromat TIRF objective with 1.49 numerical aperture.
Bring the microscope into TIRF configuration.
Adjust the excitation laser to be off-centered when hitting the back aperture of the TIRF objective.
Keep adjusting the laser until the critical angle is reached and the laser is being reflected back.
Search for a cell with several gold particles in view.
Set a region of interest that encloses the cell and the gold particles.
Engage the autofocus system to correct for sample drift in the z-direction if available.
Adjust the focus manually throughout the acquisition if the image goes out of focus.
Begin acquisition with the 405 nm laser off and the 561 nm laser on.
Turn on the 405 nm laser at the lowest factory power setting if necessary activation is not occurring.
Gradually increase 405 nm laser power until several tens of molecules per frame are visible or single molecules are well separated.
Continue to gradually increase 405 nm laser power as acquisition continues to maintain a constant spot density.
Increase the 405 nm excitation power until high power (2.5 – 10 W/cm2) does not activate more activation events.
Process the images.
Download the image processing software or the latest version from the provided URL.
Open Matlab and load the wfiread software (which is already put in the default path).
View the raw image sequence and determine the region of interest.
Select the area of the stack to be processed by left clicking and dragging a box around the desired area.
If the region of interest was not reduced during acquisition, select a smaller area to lessen the compute time.
To deselect an area and process the entire frame, right click anywhere in the image.
Select a gold particle by left clicking on the image and dragging a small box around it.
Under Particle Tracking, click the Track button to track the selected gold particle across the stack of images.
Repeat this process to track as many gold particles as possible and determine the ones that track together.
Individually select the gold particles that tracked together one at a time and click the Add Marker button under Particle Tracking.
Adjust the Sigma Range, Smoothing Range and Threshold as necessary by changing the values slightly.
Click the Find Particle button to test the settings.
The particles that will be processed will be boxed and those that are not will be left out.
Start processing the images by clicking the Make Coord File button.
Save the file.
Launch the ‘palm’ package in Matlab.
Load the .cor file created from processed single molecule images.
Sort individual coordinates using Combining Frame - 8, Combining Distance (nm) - 100, Minimum RMS - 4, Minimum Fit Goodness - 0.25, and Max. Eccentricity - 1.4 for PAmCherry1.
Generate a new set of sorted coordinates ready for rendering high resolution images by clicking the Sort button.
Enter raw pixel size (nm), desired feature size (nm) in rendered image, and pixel size for the rendered image for proper image rendering.
Treat the tissue culture surface as described in Protocol 2.
Plate the cells according to Protocol 2 instructions.
Ensure the coverglass has an appropriate thickness of 0.17 mm for the microscopy setup.
Transfect cells if conducting a transient expression experiment.
Perform necessary treatments, such as tetracycline induction, and incubate accordingly.
Place the culture dish on an on-stage incubator.
Let the dish stabilize on the stage until temperature and CO2 concentration are stable after mounting or changing regions of interest.
Block lasers at this step to prevent phototoxicity.
If CO2 control is unavailable, switch to a CO2-independent medium immediately before imaging.
Use phenol-red-free medium to reduce background fluorescence.
Acquire images as detailed in Protocol 2.
Set an appropriate exposure time (typically 25-50 msec for PAmCherry1).
Maintain molecule density lower than that of fixed cells to avoid overlapping trajectories.
Set the 561 nm laser power density to 0.8 kW/cm² for optimal signal-to-noise ratio and reduced phototoxicity, extending trajectory length.
Process the images.
Extract coordinates of single molecules with the wfiread package as described in Protocol 2, or with another package.
Reconstruct single particle trajectories using various single particle tracking (SPT) packages based on different algorithms found elsewhere.
Calculate displacement and diffusion constants from the trajectories using an SPT package.
Determine diffusion states of the target proteins using variational Bayes single-particle tracking (vbSPT).
